papers.source_abstract: Abstract High-precision sensing of interfacial motion has attracted great attention due to its vital role in intelligent microrobotics. However, it is still challenging to develop flexible sensors capable of both multiscenario detection and motion mode identification. Here, we report a flexible magnetic tactile sensor (FMTS) that mimics the hierarchical microsetae of Porthesia similis larvae in nature. When the hierarchical hair array is bent under force, the Hall component detects the tiny changes in the magnetic field due to the rearrangement of internal NdFeB microparticles. The FMTS reaches a maximum sensitivity of 22.02 μT/mN, a high resolution of 0.1 mN, and a linear working range of 0 to 46.26 mN. Diverse multiscenario perceptions are demonstrated, including solid morphology recognition, liquid flow velocity measurement, biological signal monitoring, identification of relative motion mode (e.g., rotation or slippage), and real-time motion monitoring of the grasped objects. This framework advances multiscenario perception in robotic interactions.

papers.source_abstract: Abstract Nociceptors which detect pain against harmful stimuli, exhibit region-dependent sensitivity, leading to variations in perceived pain intensity across different parts of the body. Herein, we propose region-dependent nociceptive responses emulated by reflecting difference of activated number of fibers through low-pain-mimicking synaptic transistor (LST) and high-pain-mimicking synaptic transistor (HST), each characterized by distinct synaptic weights. The variation in synaptic weight is achieved by modulating the charge-trapping capability of high-k HfOX, precisely controlled by ultraviolet treatment time. Under 64 consecutive spike inputs, the LST and HST exhibited average post-synaptic current variations of 135.4% and 264.4%, respectively, across device-to-device measurements. The back of the hand and the calf, which exhibit different pressure pain thresholds, were taken as representative examples to demonstrate that the perceived pain intensity differs across body regions in response to identical stimulus magnitudes. These results validate their capability to emulate region-dependent variations in pain perception across body regions. Furthermore, these results demonstrate that key nociceptive characteristics such as threshold behavior, no adaptation, and sensitization exhibit different firing points depending on the magnitude of the applied stimulus, and that the onset of these characteristics also varies with stimulus frequency. Furthermore, to more realistically emulate nociceptive characteristics of the human body, a region-dependent artificial pain perception system was developed by integrating a force-sensitive resistor sensor, an Arduino-based signal processor, and synaptic transistors. Through this region-dependent artificial pain perception system, realistic pain-like sensory feedback was achieved while emulating sensitization phenomena such as allodynia and hyperalgesia, demonstrating a hardware-level implementation that reproduces region-dependent pain transmission observed in the human body and offering significant potential for neuroprosthetics, robotics, and e-skin applications.

papers.source_abstract: Abstract Stretchable materials are essential for wearable bioelectronic applications. However, current strategies still remain challenging to achieve fully integrated stretchable bioelectronic devices due to the limited electrical functionality and the complex fabrication processes of stretchable materials. Here, we develop metallic nanowire film hierarchical structures for multifunctional stretchable bioelectronic systems. The hierarchical structures show the application-specific functions of high conductivity (3.84 × 106 S/m at 30% of strain), electromechanical sensitivity, and electrocatalytic performance (60.06 μA/cm2/mM of sensitivity for glucose) by the combination of metallic nanowire and films. Moreover, micropatterned hierarchical structures at a width of 50 μm exhibit low device-to-device variations in resistance (<20%). This unified material platform enables simplified fabrication workflow, maintaining its electrical characteristics and stretchability. As a model system, the fully integrated wireless smart contact lenses with the hierarchical structures demonstrate the stable operation for continuous intraocular pressure and glucose monitoring under ocular deformation in rabbit models, reflecting the feasibility for various bioelectronic applications.

papers.source_abstract: Abstract Acute compartment syndrome (ACS) requires timely diagnosis, delayed diagnosis can cause irreversible neuromuscular injury, limb loss, and even death, whereas current diagnosis still relies on subjective examination and intermittent invasive pressure measurements. Here, we report an injectable, biodegradable biotelemetric implant for accurate, continuous wireless monitoring of intracompartmental pressure (IcP), and further establish a predictive model that converts pressure-duration signals into quantitative assessment of ACS progression, providing a clinically relevant framework for diagnosis and intervention. Our platform integrates an ultraminiaturized iontronic pressure transducer as the implant with a parity-time symmetric wireless readout circuit, enabling precise sensing and mapping of pressure-time load onto a two-dimensional ACS matrix for quantitative prediction of disease progression. The device functions throughout the clinically relevant monitoring window and then degrades naturally, eliminating the need for retrieval surgery. This work offers a transient, minimally invasive strategy for continuous ACS surveillance, and highlights the translational potential of biodegradable implantable bioelectronics for trauma care.

papers.source_abstract: ABSTRACT Organic thermoelectric materials hold immense promises for wearable electronic devices, offering the potential to harness body heat for power generation. However, the interdependence of thermoelectric performance parameters, resulting in relatively low overall performance, remains a major limitation for power generation applications. In this study, a series of novel diradical spiro molecules are synthesized and integrated with single‐wall carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) as p ‐ and n ‐type thermoelectric materials. Diradical spiro molecules leverage synergistic advantages of radical structures and spiro cross‐conjugated backbones. Radical structures align molecular energy levels with SWCNTs, facilitating electron transfer. Spiro cross‐conjugated backbone strengthens molecular adsorption on SWCNTs, achieving excellent dispersion and strong interactions in carbon nanotube networks. This dual strategy enables simultaneous optimization of three key thermoelectric parameters, leading to significant enhancement in thermoelectric performance. The SFX2‐PO •• /SWCNT composites, where the SFX2‐PO •• molecule possesses a spiro[dibenzo[c,h]xanthene‐7,9′‐fluorene] (SFX2) core and bis(2,6‐di‐ tert ‐butylphenoxy radical) (PO •• ) substituents, exhibit the highest power factors among both p ‐ and n ‐type materials, attributed to its highest doping level and strongest interaction energy. The corresponding thermoelectric generators show reliable sensitivity to low‐grade heat sources such as human skin, together with mechanical, thermal, and air stability, underscoring their strong potential for wearable and portable energy harvesting applications.

papers.source_abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries with hydrogel electrolytes have attracted considerable attention for wearable energy‐storage devices owing to their intrinsic safety and mechanical flexibility. However, conventional hydrogel electrolytes often exhibit limited rate capability and environmental adaptability, which are closely related to the decoupled regulation of ion transport and interfacial chemistry. To overcome these limitations, a spatially cooperative electrolyte‐engineering approach was developed through constructing a co‐crosslinked network ( p (AM‐ co ‐VIB)) through the copolymerization of acrylamide (AM) and 1‐vinyl‐3‐butylimidazolium bromide (VIB), while introducing 3‐(N,N‐dimethylmyristylammonio) propane sulfonate (ST) to construct a hydrogel electrolyte (PV‐S). The p (AM‐ co ‐VIB) network provides efficient ion‐transport pathways and structural robustness, while the ST‐derived zincophilic‐hydrophobic domains regulate the local Zn 2+ coordination environment, promoting homogeneous Zn 2+ distribution and confining interfacial water. Consequently, the PV‐S electrolyte delivers an average coulombic efficiency of 99.57%. Furthermore, the Zn||Zn symmetric cells sustain highly reversible Zn plating/stripping across a broad current‐density range of 1–40 mA cm −2 . Notably, stable operation can be maintained over a wide temperature window (−40°C to 80°C), with prolonged cycling exceeding 2800 h at −20°C. Additionally, the Zn||NVO full cell retains 82.4% capacity retention over 850 cycles. Remarkably, the Zn||NVO pouch cell with a limited N/P ratio (3.9) retains 92.1% capacity after 220 cycles.

papers.source_abstract: ABSTRACT Intrinsically stretchable organic solar cells (IS‐OSCs) hold great promise for wearable electronics, yet their development is severely hindered by the trade‐off between efficiency and mechanical robustness, remaining a critical challenge. Herein, three polymerized small‐molecule acceptors (PSMAs) with distinct molecular topologies: linear PYIT, star‐shaped BTPPYIT, and dimer‐star‐shaped 2BTPPYIT were synthesized with different free volume ratio (FVR), following the order of PYIT > BTPPYIT > 2BTPPYIT. The FVR can acts as a detector to reflect intermolecular interactions and chain entanglement, thereby governing the balance between photovoltaic and mechanical properties. Among these polymers, the star‐shaped BTPPYIT with suitable FVR enables most optimal film morphology for efficient charge transport, while possesses strong chain entanglement for mechanical stretchability. Consequently, the BTPPYIT‐based binary device achieves a record efficiency of 17.36% among star‐shaped PSMAs, and a ternary device reaches a high efficiency of 20.05%. Notably, the BTPPYIT‐based IS‐OSCs achieve both a high efficiency of 12.58% and excellent stretchability (80% PCE retention at 22.65% strain), representing one of the best comprehensive performances reported for IS‐OSCs. Overall, the star‐shaped architecture of BTPPYIT with suitable FVR is very effective for decoupling the efficiency‐flexibility trade‐off in stretchable organic electronics.

Here, we report a molecular design strategy based on proton–ion cooperative interactions to construct a reconfigurable polar network in a transparent polyelectrolyte hydrogel. By incorporating polymerizable choline–proline ionic liquids (CPILs) into a hydrogen‐bonded poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) matrix, the spatial distribution and orientation dynamics of polar moieties are regulated through synergistic covalent and dynamic noncovalent interactions. These proton–ion cooperative interactions enable simultaneous enhancement of dielectric polarization and interfacial adhesion within a single transparent network. Consequently, the hydrogel achieves an effective electromagnetic absorption bandwidth of 6.5 GHz and a minimum reflection loss of −49.31 dB, while maintaining an average visible‐light transmittance exceeding 96% and a shear adhesion strength of 7.71 MPa on glass substrates. This work establishes a molecular‐level design paradigm for coupling dielectric polarization and interfacial adhesion in transparent soft materials, providing new opportunities for flexible electronics and transparent electromagnetic wave absorption.

papers.source_abstract: Flexible electronics (FEs) have the potential to endow objects with the virtues and functionalities of electronics. The key is transferring manufactured FEs from original rigid substrates and printing onto targets. However, existing transfer printing accommodates limited circumstances due to immutable mechanical properties of either solid or liquid stamps. Here, a self-adaptive, configurable transfer printing method is developed based on the unique rheology of liquid foam that enables integration of ultrathin FEs onto arbitrary surfaces conformally, three-dimensionally and non-invasively. The liquid foam exhibits adaptive mechanical properties between solid and liquid, converting among elastic, plastic and dynamic behaviors spontaneously. We demonstrate liquid foam can support FEs with shape maintained prepared with no defect, transform FEs to irregular topographies in a stress-free manner, and extend the reach of FEs to inner surfaces of semi-closed objects i.e., cranial cavity, which were barely feasible before. This approach overcomes key bottlenecks of current technologies and opens numerous opportunities for FEs in wearables and brain-computer interfaces.

papers.source_abstract: ABSTRACT Traditional hydrogel dressings face challenges like poor adhesion and limited antibacterial effects. We developed a biocompatible polyacrylamide‐DNA double‐network hydrogel (AuPt/PEDOT–DNA gel), cross‐linked by bis‐acrylamide and DNA duplexes, offering softness, stretchability, and self‐adhesiveness for direct skin application. Incorporating AuPt/PEDOT, a cascade nanozyme with peroxidase/oxidase‐mimicking activities and high photothermal efficiency, enables dual antibacterial action via ROS generation and photothermal therapy. Under near‐infrared irradiation, it achieves > 95% bacterial killing at safe concentrations and inhibits biofilm formation. Moreover, the intrinsic conductivity of the AuPt/PEDOT–DNA gel enables its operation as a flexible strain sensor that transduces skin deformation into motion signals, which can be harnessed to monitor periwound mechanical strain and provide active feedback to prevent excessive tissue tension, thereby complementing the antimicrobial and drug‐delivery functions with biomechanical protection during rehabilitation. It conforms to wounds, prevents drug leakage, and eradicates bacteria, enhancing prospects for advanced hydrogel dressings.
